slides.title: Adding the Practical Skill Layer
bullets: Scientific exchange is genuine, balanced, non-promotional dialogue about science
This module adds the conversational techniques behind that definition
The gap: exchange that generates insight and trust versus exchange that is only technically compliant

slides.title: The Ingredients Experts Agree On
bullets: Careful preparation with a clear purpose
Thoughtfully crafted open-ended questions
Active listening
Adjusting the conversation dynamically, not running a fixed script

slides.title: Same Script, Every Conversation
bullets: Many technically strong MSLs run every visit the same way
They know the data perfectly but not how to adapt to the person
Misses whether the expert wants deep statistics, clinical application, or space to raise concerns first

slides.title: Only Two Modes Belong Here
bullets: The spectrum: informing, persuading, exploring and co-creating
Informing and exploring belong in genuine scientific exchange
Persuading crosses into promotional territory
Co-creating is reserved for advisory boards and investigator collaborations

slides.title: Exchange Has a Shape Over Time
bullets: Skilled MSLs do not treat each visit as a self-contained event
They reference and deepen prior conversations
They track open questions across visits
What they remember and follow up on proves the relationship is cumulative

takeaway.title: Scientific exchange is a practical skill built on preparation, real listening and honest limits
bullets: Genuine exchange requires purpose, open questions, listening and adaptability
Only informing and exploring belong in routine scientific exchange
Good exchange builds a relationship across visits, not a single conversation
